metrics.financial: Managed $10k+ rapid prototyping budget for high-pressure trade show build; negotiated short-run fab costs (e.g., $242.35/cover for zinc-plated revisions).
metrics.process: Reduced complex sheet metal fabrication cycle to 9 days; Standardized 100% of assembly hardware to 4-40 spec to eliminate line-down risks.
metrics.governance: Orchestrated parallel workstreams between sheet metal (E-M Solutions) and model shops (Sputnik) under a high-velocity 'War Room' cadence.

forensic_summary: TRIGGER: The 'Elmer' main board relied on an aluminum heat spreader requiring a 'dead nuts flat' chassis for thermal conduction, a tolerance impossibility for sheet metal. Simultaneously, a 'screw-up' on the prototype build mixed metric and SAE hardware, threatening assembly yield. INTERVENTION: Norris ('The Architect') rejected the 'Bastard Box' concept, executing a custom chassis design that removed perforation under the PCB for mass conduction while forcing convective airflow near the PSU. He enforced a strict 4-40 UNC hardware standardization for the 'Zeus' revision. RESULT: Delivery of 5 functional server enclosures and 12 nodes for Western Cable Show and CES 2001 on a compressed 9-day fabrication cycle with zero thermal failures.
